basic_identification.full_title: Identification of Parts for Complete, Filled Transport Packages when Testing (First Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Transport Engineering / Transport Packaging and Pallets (approved by the Marine, Cargo Movement and Packaging Division Council and finalized by the Transport Packages Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies a standardized, uniform system for identifying the different parts (surfaces, edges, and corners) of complete, filled transport packages when undergoing mechanical, physical, or environmental testing. It covers parallelepipedal (box-shaped) packages, cylindrical packages, sacks and bags, and miscellaneous packages.

revision_history.edition: First Edition (published under the title 'Method for Identification of Parts for Complete, Filled Transport Packages')
First Revision (reorganized and aligned with ISO 2206:1987 to expand the scope to cover sacks, bags, and miscellaneous shapes, and provide a standardized reference system)

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Procedural and Testing Specification (Transport Engineering / Package Testing)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Procedural Standard (Transport Packaging). Since IS 7030 is an engineering methodology code rather than a consumer product, it is certified on a voluntary basis under BIS schemes. However, compliance with its structural designs, material thickness categories, air-tight joints, vaned grids, and support brackets is universally mandated inside all national public, defense, Indian Navy, port authority, and commercial shipyard procurement contracts to ensure air-tightness and corrosion protection.

requirements.detail: Requires placing the package in its intended transport position. If unknown, arbitrarily select one. If a manufacturer's joint exists, it must be placed vertically on the observer's right. With one side facing the observer, identify surfaces as: No. 1 (Top), No. 2 (Right), No. 3 (Bottom), No. 4 (Left), No. 5 (Nearest / Front), and No. 6 (Farthest away / Rear). If more than one manufacturer's joint exists, arbitrarily select one end as No. 5.
Edges are designated by combining the numbers of the two meeting surfaces. For example, edge '1-2' identifies the line formed by the meeting of the top surface (No. 1) and the right surface (No. 2).
Corners are designated by combining the numbers of the three meeting surfaces. For example, corner '1-2-5' identifies the point where the top (No. 1), right (No. 2), and front (No. 5) surfaces meet.

The ends of two perpendicular diameters on the upper surface of the cylinder are designated as 1, 3, 5, and 7. The corresponding parallel lines along the cylinder axis are designated as 2, 4, 6, and 8 respectively. The axial lines connecting them are designated as lines 1-2, 3-4, 5-6, and 7-8. If a manufacturer's joint exists, it should occupy the position 5-6.

requirements.requirement_type: Sacks and Bags Positioning and Orientation
requirements.detail: The sack or bag is placed flat on one face with its sealed/bottom end towards the observer. Any side seam must be positioned on the observer's right. If two side seams exist, one must be on the right and the other on the left. If a longitudinal seam exists, it must face downwards, with the top (filling end) of the sack pointing away from the observer. Surfaces are then identified systematically starting from the uppermost face.

Irregularly shaped packages must be arbitrarily mapped using analogous designations derived from the basic parallelepipedal or cylindrical models, with all reference numbers and selected orientations fully documented in the testing report.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 7030 : 1988 is the mandatory national Indian Standard code of practice specifying a standardized method for identifying the various parts—specifically the surfaces, edges, and corners—of complete, filled transport packages when undergoing mechanical or environmental testing. Strictly required for recording tested attitudes and damage locations in all packaging evaluations (such as IS 7028 stack, drop, and vibration tests), this standard establishes a uniform numbering system. For example, in box-shaped (parallelepipedal) packages, it numbers surfaces 1 through 6 (Top, Right, Bottom, Left, Front, Rear) based on intended transport position and manufacturer's joint location, while defining clear rules for mapping cylindrical drums, paper or plastic sacks, bags, and irregularly shaped cargo containers to ensure clear, repeatable test reporting across the shipping and logistics sectors.
